performance.overall_assessment:
One new blocking performance finding: the shared outbound resolver has a global unindexed reverse-identity lookup (NUM-PERF-01). No additional concrete request amplification, provider page walking, fetch-all scheduler reconciliation or newly introduced exhaustion path was established. This is an independent read-only performance/PCV judgment of the frozen ST-CON-01 local delivery, not a production or final security/TQA verdict. Routing evidence declares formal-reviewer gpt-6.1-sol/max and GO. I directly read the present new/untracked implementation and relevant manifest-allowed consumers, controllers, schema/migrations, provider adapters, frontend operation owner/polling, PCV/browser harnesses, runner/runtime configuration and the governing TODO/module/pcv-1 references. I independently verified 266 manifest/index reference entries with zero hash mismatches, including all214 frozen public-source entries (213 present and the approved absent slug-only spec), indexed artifacts/canon and supplementary API build references. No private dotenv, operational Git blobs or .local-files payloads were read or hashed; no tests, builds, runtime/provider probes or mutations were run for this review.

Access-path and budget assessment: registration reads by attempt id plus tenant, idempotency replay by the composite unique key, channel slots by buId/type (maximum two channel types per BU), credentials by unique channelId, webhook resource mapping and message dedupe by composite unique keys are structurally bounded apart from NUM-PERF-01. Business-unit lists project local channels and make no provider calls. The existing user-grant/tenant BU collections and tenant-scoped Typebot trigger matching remain proportional to their authorized sets; the touched Typebot change narrows tenant scope and does not justify an unrelated architecture rewrite. No new scheduler, hydration cache, outbox or global reconciliation worker was introduced; the nearby webhook purge retains bounded1000-row batches/100-batch cap. BFF/public sends make one explicit adapter send; Typebot's per-response message loop retains approved behavior and is triggered only for the winning accepted IN. MessageAcceptance uses the PostgreSQL resource/externalId unique key, identity fence through commit and BU/contact advisory locking, limiting duplicate Message/unread/realtime/bot effects rather than retrying remote sends.

Provider operations were inspected beyond fake-port call totals: authorize is exchange plus token debug (two HTTP requests); options is one token debug and optionally one explicitly requested phone page; confirm is token debug plus the selected page and optionally one register (maximum three); advance/retry has one subscription operation, and ambiguous register/subscription/code exchange never replays automatically. Meta pages request limit100 and use an explicit cursor limited to512 characters; no remote next URL is followed. Evolution uses the named instanceName filter in one fetchInstances request and checks the exact name. Pairing worst-case create/lookup/QR combinations have at most three requests, while old-instance cleanup uses at most lookup+delete and returns before creating a replacement in a later round. Verify uses at most two Meta reads or one Evolution lookup; disconnect cleanup uses at most lookup+delete. Each adapter fetch has a ten-second AbortSignal timeout and rejects redirects; per-channel CAS leases are45 seconds. HTTP occurs outside DB transactions, and current attempt/generation/epoch/lease/session/grant are rechecked around provider work. These are local budget and fencing properties, not provider exactly-once guarantees.
